open_questions: Depth scatter between sectors and low SNR (16.17) dip with only 4 transits 3 near a gap and one strong outlier needs additional TESS or follow-up transits to confirm consistency
xgboost planet_rank 0.32 is below median 0.5 but only one planet in ten scores this low; follow-up transit photometry and radial velocity will test mass

Rotation period 7.563d is 1.8998942218696284x the 14.4d period and variability amplitude 2846-5360 ppm is large for Teff 4279K; spot crossings could explain depth variation but should be checked with multicolor photometry
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 1,130 ppm, 3.5-hour flat-bottom transit every 14.4 days on a nearby small star, implying a ~2.5 Earth-radius candidate in an orbit that fits the star. There is no significant secondary eclipse, no nearby star that could mimic the dip, and no Gaia sign of a binary. The dip appears a little deeper in one sector and is near the star's 7.6-day spot signal, but the shape and size are planet-like and the best explanation remains a small planet pending additional transits.

reasons.why: Flat-bottomed transit morphology supports planet over V-shaped grazing EB; fit_b 0.102, central duration fit excellent.
No sector has a clear difference image, so centroid does not show off-target, and neighbours.plausible_within_1px 0 rules out a close blended neighbour despite could_cause 5 at >50 arcsec.
Observed 3.499h matches central 3.392h for 0.6724 Rsun dwarf (duration.ratio 1.032, stellar_radius fit_b 0.102), implying small Rp 2.47 Rearth that favours planet.
Odd/even difference 445.1 ppm not significant at 4 sigma, and sector_oe_max_sigma 5.256 occurs in only 1 sector with 0.5 same-sign share, no consistent binary at twice period.

No secondary detection (best_brightening_snr 4.205 > 3.289, depth_over_dip 0.1648, sector_sec_half_max_snr -0.7664), and star binary flags non_single_star 0, ruwe 0.8933 show no Gaia companion, consistent with planet.

Depth changes 1370 +/-130 ppm in SPOC 2-min sector 2 vs 862 +/-114 ppm in TESS-SPOC sector 69 with only one sector per source; Moon-affected sector 2 and spot activity (rotation amplitude 2846-5360 ppm) offer plausible astrophysical explanations for the scatter rather than a blend, and transit depths are individually 1120 ppm mean with one 264 ppm outlier at -4.9 sigma.
